scenes.visual: Title card: A Route in Legs.

scenes.tts: The first axons start out through the far end of a growing leg. No earlier axons lie ahead of them. How do they find the way?
scenes.visual: A schematic grasshopper embryo leg (labelled AI illustration). Two neurons at the tip send out axons into the empty distal part of the leg; the region nearer the body is out of frame. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: The first axons start out through the far end of a growing leg. No earlier axons lie ahead of them. How do they find the way?

scenes.tts: The moving tip of a growing axon is the growth cone. It does not carry a map.
scenes.visual: Close-up of a growth cone: a fan of actin with finger-like filopodia, microtubules running back into the axon shaft. A crossed-out map icon.
scenes.narration: The moving tip of a growing axon is the growth cone. It does not carry a map.

scenes.tts: It is roughly ten micrometres across, and its filopodia reach farther. It can touch what lies against it.
scenes.caption: It is roughly 10 µm across, and its filopodia reach farther. It can touch what lies against it.
scenes.visual: Scale bar: about 10 µm across the growth cone; filopodia extend beyond it. Filopodia touch a surface and light up where they make contact.
scenes.narration: It is roughly 10 µm across, and its filopodia reach farther. It can touch what lies against it.

scenes.tts: And it can compare how much of a cue reaches its two sides.
scenes.visual: A faint cloud of cue molecules, denser on one side of the growth cone. The two sides are labelled more and less.
scenes.narration: And it can compare how much of a cue reaches its two sides.

scenes.tts: Take the simplest case. One cell releases an attractant into uniform tissue. The growth cone heads straight up its gradient.
scenes.visual: One source cell in the centre, a shaded gradient fading outward evenly. A growth cone sits some distance away. Corner label: Ideal model.
scenes.narration: Take the simplest case. One cell releases an attractant into uniform tissue. The growth cone heads straight up its gradient.

scenes.tts: What shape is the path?
scenes.visual: The growth cone waits. On-screen text: What shape is the path?
scenes.narration: What shape is the path?

scenes.visual: Hold on the source and the waiting growth cone. A small timer icon.

scenes.tts: A straight line to the source. In this ideal case, the cue falls off equally in every direction.
scenes.visual: The growth cone runs in a straight line to the source. Concentric rings show the cue falling off equally all round. Corner label: Ideal radial-gradient model.
scenes.narration: A straight line to the source. In this ideal case, the cue falls off equally in every direction.

scenes.tts: So uphill always points at the source. And at the source, the climb ends.
scenes.visual: Three growth cones start from different places. All three run straight to the source, like spokes, and stop there.
scenes.narration: So uphill always points at the source. And at the source, the climb ends.

scenes.tts: Add a second source, and the path can curve. Where it ends depends on where it starts.
scenes.visual: A second source appears. One growth cone follows a curve to one source. Label: One possible trajectory.
scenes.narration: Add a second source, and the path can curve. Where it ends depends on where it starts.

scenes.tts: Either way, an attractant gives a destination, not a list of stops.
scenes.visual: On-screen text: an attractant gives a destination, not a list of stops.
scenes.narration: Either way, an attractant gives a destination, not a list of stops.

scenes.visual: Hold on the curved path ending at its source.

scenes.tts: Real routes reach a place and go on from it. The first axons out of an insect leg make several sharp turns.
scenes.visual: A limb outline with the real route drawn in: a path with several sharp turns. Label: real route.
scenes.narration: Real routes reach a place and go on from it. The first axons out of an insect leg make several sharp turns.

scenes.tts: A turn like that usually means the growth cone has started reading something new.
scenes.visual: A turn on the route is circled. Label: usually, something new is read here.
scenes.narration: A turn like that usually means the growth cone has started reading something new.

scenes.tts: A cell it touches, a boundary in the tissue, or a different cue.
scenes.visual: Three small icons at the turn: a cell, a tissue boundary line, a second cue cloud.
scenes.narration: A cell it touches, a boundary in the tissue, or a different cue.

scenes.tts: Reach adds a second limit. A secreted cue thins as it spreads.
scenes.visual: A cue cloud fades with distance from its source. A growth cone moves further away.
scenes.narration: Reach adds a second limit. A secreted cue thins as it spreads.

scenes.tts: Far enough away, the difference across a growth cone is lost in noise.
scenes.visual: Far from the source, the small difference between the two sides of the growth cone is swamped by flickering noise. Label: lost in noise.
scenes.narration: Far enough away, the difference across a growth cone is lost in noise.

scenes.tts: Simple models with plausible values put that at hundreds of micrometres to a few millimetres. It is an estimate, not a fixed range.
scenes.visual: Range card: hundreds of µm to a few mm. Small print beneath: simple diffusion model; depends on sensitivity, cue lifetime and receptor range. See Going deeper.
scenes.narration: Simple models with plausible values put that at hundreds of micrometres to a few millimetres. It is an estimate, not a fixed range.

scenes.tts: So here is the rule. A growth cone reads only what is within its reach.
scenes.visual: Rule card, first line: a growth cone reads only what is within its reach.
scenes.narration: So here is the rule. A growth cone reads only what is within its reach.

scenes.tts: So a long route is usually built as a chain of legs.
scenes.visual: The real route splits into coloured legs, with a dot at each turn.
scenes.narration: So a long route is usually built as a chain of legs.

scenes.tts: Each leg ends at a choice point, where the growth cone picks its next path. There it reads something new, or reads the same thing differently.
scenes.visual: Each dot is labelled choice point. Rule card, second line: at each choice point, read something new, or read the same thing differently.
scenes.narration: Each leg ends at a choice point, where the growth cone picks its next path. There it reads something new, or reads the same thing differently.

scenes.tts: At many choice points, growth cones pause and spread out before they choose.
scenes.visual: A growth cone reaches a dot, pauses, spreads its filopodia, then turns onto the next leg. Label: a common behaviour at a choice point.
scenes.narration: At many choice points, growth cones pause and spread out before they choose.

scenes.tts: Not every bend needs a new reading. A pioneer axon can lead followers around long curves.
scenes.visual: A follower axon rides along a curved pioneer axon. Takeaway card: local readings, chained at choice points; contact paths can curve.
scenes.narration: Not every bend needs a new reading. A pioneer axon can lead followers around long curves.

scenes.visual: Hold on the takeaway card.
